findings.claim: Q2's keyed answer says validating a path variable requires putting the constraint on the method parameter AND 'enable method validation on the controller' (feedback: 'with validation enabled on the class'). Since Spring Framework 6.1 (and in Framework 7 / Boot 4 as taught here), Spring MVC validates constrained handler method parameters natively, raising HandlerMethodValidationException, with no @Validated or other enabling step on the controller. The module's own bean-validation-on-requests page teaches exactly this: '@GetMapping("/workshops/{id}") Workshop one(@PathVariable @Positive long id)' ... 'That uses Spring method validation, which raises HandlerMethodValidationException'. A learner who studied the page can reasonably doubt the keyed option because of its extra required step, and its feedback reinforces an obsolete requirement.
findings.recommendation: Reword the keyed option and feedback to match the page: 'Put the constraint annotation directly on the method parameter; Spring MVC method validation rejects bad path and query values with 400' (dropping the 'enable method validation on the controller' clause).
